queries: WITH r AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_len FROM film GROUP BY rating), b AS (SELECT AVG(length) AS base FROM film), k1 AS (SELECT r.rating, r.avg_len, b.base FROM r CROSS JOIN b WHERE r.avg_len > b.base), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_len) AS mean_kept FROM k1), k2 AS (SELECT k1.avg_len, k1.base, m.mean_kept FROM k1 CROSS JOIN m WHERE k1.avg_len > m.mean_kept) SELECT AVG(avg_len) AS mean_avg_length, AVG(avg_len - base) AS mean_excess_over_baseline, AVG(avg_len - mean_kept) AS mean_excess_over_kept_mean FROM k2

assumptions.assumption: The baseline is the film-level average length over all films (each film counting equally, NULL lengths ignored), not the average of the per-rating averages.

The 'kept ratings' mean' in the third output column is the mean of the first-stage kept ratings' averages, which is the mean used for the second filter. It is not the mean of the final remaining ratings.
Ratings are grouped as stored. The verified data shows 5 distinct values, so no ratings need merging.

assumptions.assumption: The baseline is the plain average of length over all films with a non-null length (each film counts equally), not the average of the rating averages.
The 'mean of their average lengths' is the unweighted mean of the per-rating averages for the ratings that passed the first filter. The second filter is strict (>), and so is the first.

assumptions.assumption: The baseline is the plain average of film.length over all films with a non-null length. Each film counts once, not each rating.

"The kept ratings' mean" in the third output is the mean of the average lengths of the ratings that passed the baseline filter. This is the same mean used for the second filter. It is not the mean of the final remaining ratings, which would make the result trivially 0.
